Wellness Coordinator (Adolescent Mental Health Technician)

On-Site | Boca Raton, FL | Part-Time | $18/hour
Schedule: Monday–Friday, 3:00 PM–8:00 PM

About the Role

Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) is seeking a Bilingual Wellness Coordinator / Mental Health Technician to support adolescents ages 13–17 in our PHP and IOP mental health programs.

This hands-on role focuses on behavioral health support, client supervision, crisis de-escalation, safety monitoring, and daily program operations.

Relevant backgrounds: Mental Health Technician · Behavioral Health · Youth Services · Psychology · Social Work · Education

What You'll Do

  • Supervise adolescents during programming, breaks, and transitions.
  • Monitor client safety and support behavioral de-escalation.
  • Assist clinicians with therapeutic schedules and group activities.
  • Coordinate client check-in, dismissal, and family communication.
  • Manage attendance, front desk tasks, and program logistics.
  • Complete daily documentation, wellness checks, and incident reports.
  • Report behavioral concerns and safety risks to clinical staff.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • Bilingual English/Spanish.
  • Experience with adolescents in behavioral health, education, or youth services.
  • Strong communication, documentation, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to manage challenging behaviors calmly and professionally.
  • Availability Monday–Friday, 3:00 PM–8:00 PM.

Preferred

  • Mental health technician, behavioral health, or crisis intervention experience.
  • Education in Psychology, Counseling, Social Work, or related fields.
  • Experience in PHP, IOP, or adolescent mental health settings.

About AWA

Adolescent Wellness Academy provides compassionate mental health treatment for adolescents through PHP and IOP programs. Join a team dedicated to creating a safe, supportive environment where teens can grow and thrive.

Learn More: Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
